source.name: A dialog created with keyboard: false must stay open however often Escape is pressed
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/43070) at 2bb544eb426e9b1e019c2a98798e0002b8a41d35, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

journey.title: Escape must not dismiss a dialog opened with keyboard: false
journey.goal: The confirmation dialog stays open however often Escape is pressed, so the user can still enter the code and send the transfer

functionalJourney.title: Confirm with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking the backdrop does not close the dialog; entering the code and clicking Send completes the transfer

guards.title: Cancel transfer still closes the dialog from the keyboard
guards.goal: Tabbing to Cancel transfer and pressing Enter closes the dialog and records the cancellation

plan.root_cause: The Escape key handler for modal dialogs relies exclusively on the native 'cancel' event. After repeated Escape presses, the cancel event loses its cancelability (becomes non‑cancelable), so the listener's preventDefault() no longer stops the dialog from closing. The separate keydown listener for Escape only runs for non‑modal dialogs, leaving modal dialogs without a fallback when the cancel event fails.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the Escape keydown listener in DialogBase to ignore the openedAsModal check, allowing it to run for modal dialogs as well. When keyboard is false, the listener triggers the static backdrop transition (mirroring the cancel listener) and prevents default; otherwise it proceeds to cancel and hide. This ensures Escape is always handled regardless of the cancel event's cancelability.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will no longer dismiss the dialog when keyboard:false, allowing users to press Escape repeatedly to dismiss backdrop animations without losing focus or closing the dialog. This preserves keyboard operability (WCAG 2.1.1) and ensures the dialog remains accessible until explicit cancellation or submission.
functional_risks: Double handling of Escape (both cancel and keydown listeners) may trigger redundant backdrop transitions, but this is harmless as the transition is idempotent.
The dialog's hide logic is guarded against multiple calls via _isTransitioning and _canHide, so no risk of premature closure.
No change to modal behavior when keyboard:true; Escape will still close the dialog as expected.
verification_requirements: Press Escape multiple times while the dialog is open with keyboard:false; the dialog must remain open and focus must stay within the dialog.
Press Escape once with keyboard:true; the dialog must close.
After repeated Escape presses with keyboard:false, entering a valid OTP and pressing Send must still succeed.
Verify that the static backdrop transition occurs on Escape when keyboard:false (visual flash or class addition).
